div.head: V Atr 30
div.ab: ⁊ gyf hwa ymb cyninges feorh syrwe, sy he his feores scyldig; ⁊ gif he ladian wille, do þæt be ðæs cynges wergylde oððe mid þryfealdan ordale on Engla lage.
⁊ gif hwa ymbe cyninges feorh syrwe, sy he his feores scyldig; ⁊ gif he ladigan wille, do þæt be þæs cynge wyrgylde oððe mid þryfealdan ordale on Engla lage.
⁊ gif hwa ymbe cyninc sirewe, beo his feores scildig, buton he hine ladige be þam deopestan þe witan gerædan.
And if anyone plots against the king, he shall forfeit his life, unless he clears himself by the most solemn oath determined upon by the authorities.

Und wenn jemand nach dem Leben des Königs trachtet, sei er [des Verlustes] seines Lebens schuldig; und (ausser D) wenn er sich [von der Anklage] reinigen will, thue er das [durch Eid] in Höhe von des Königs Wergeld oder durch dreifaches Ordal nach Engländer-Recht (durch den schwersten [Beweis], den die Witan [des Gerichts] bestimmen D).

And if anyone plots against the king's life, let him be liable [to lose] his life; and if he wishes to clear himself (unless, D), let him do so [by oath] to the amount of the king's wergild, or by the threefold ordeal according to English law (by the heaviest [proof], which the witan [of the court] decide, D).
div.note: K had ‘feoh’ (money) for ‘feorh’ (life). G2 adds two lines in the upper margin (12th c.), largely cut away by the binder. Liebermann compares Af 4, 4.1.
